screens.name: Complaints Inbox
screens.purpose: Lists every open complaint assigned to the handler's team, sorted by SLA remaining, so a handler can pick the next one to work.

screens.name: Complaint Detail
screens.purpose: Shows one complaint's customer details, its timeline of events and the handler's notes, and lets the handler add notes or change the category.

screens.name: Decision
screens.purpose: Records the outcome of the investigation (uphold, partially uphold or reject) with a reason and a written summary of findings.

screens.name: Redress
screens.purpose: Calculates the money owed to the customer (refund plus simple interest) for an upheld or partially upheld complaint and lets the handler approve it.

screens.name: Letter Preview
screens.purpose: Shows the final response letter with merge fields filled from the complaint, decision and redress, and lets the handler send it.

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: Gives the team lead a team view of open complaints, SLA breaches, uphold rate and complaints received by month, with an export to spreadsheet.

actions.description: Clicks a column header to sort the inbox; most people sort by SLA remaining
Double-clicks a row (or presses the row's Open button) to open the complaint
Types a note in the box and presses Add note; the note is stamped with the handler's name and date
Presses Change next to Category to correct the category (a note saying why must be added)
Picks Decision in the left navigation once the investigation is done
Picks an Outcome: Uphold, Partially uphold or Reject
Chooses a Reason from the dropdown and writes the Summary of findings
Presses Record decision (greyed out for trainees below grade 2)
Enters Refund amount and Days out of pocket and presses Recalculate; the system fills the Calculation table
Presses Approve redress; over £500 this raises a task for the team lead as second approver
Reads the letter through and presses Send letter; the letter goes to print (or email if the customer asked for it)
Presses Export to download the dashboard figures as a spreadsheet

journey.description: The handler lands on the Complaints Inbox, which lists the team's open complaints sorted by SLA remaining, and sorts by column if needed.
The handler double-clicks a row to open the complaint.
On Complaint Detail the handler reviews the customer details and timeline, investigates, and records what they did as notes; if the category is wrong they change it and add a note saying why.
When the investigation is done the handler goes to Decision, picks Uphold, Partially uphold or Reject, chooses a reason, writes a summary of at least 50 words and presses Record decision.

If the complaint is upheld or partially upheld the handler goes to Redress, enters the refund amount and days out of pocket, the system calculates interest and total, and the handler presses Approve redress.
If the redress is over £500 a task is raised for the team lead to give second approval.
The handler opens Letter Preview, checks the merged final response letter and presses Send letter, which sends it to print (or email if the customer asked for email).
The team lead reviews the Dashboard figures and chart and can export them as a spreadsheet.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need the Complaints Inbox to list every open complaint assigned to my team, sorted by SLA remaining by default, so that I can work the most urgent complaint first.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Handlers prioritise by time left on the 8-week deadline.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You land on the Inbox, which is every open complaint sorted by how long we've got left on it.

requirement_candidates.statement: The Complaints Inbox must show, for each complaint, the reference, customer, received date, category, status, owner and SLA remaining.
requirement_candidates.rationale: These are the columns on screen and the ones the expert names.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need to sort the inbox by clicking any column header, so that I can order the list the way I work.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You click a column header to sort, and most people sort by the SLA column.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must count down an SLA for each open complaint from the received date, with the final response due within 8 weeks of receipt, and show 'Breached' once that deadline has passed.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Footer on the inbox reads 'Final response due within 8 weeks of receipt'; SLA column shows days and hours remaining or 'Breached'.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must automatically refer any complaint older than eight weeks to the Ombudsman and set its status to Referred without any user action.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Regulatory deadline handling that the expert describes as automatic.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Anything over eight weeks old goes to the Ombudsman automatically, you'll see the status flip to Referred on its own.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need to open a complaint from the inbox by double-clicking its row (or pressing its Open button), so that I reach the Complaint Detail.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You double-click a row to open it and you get the Complaint Detail.

requirement_candidates.statement: The Complaint Detail must show the customer's name, policy, phone, email, address, received date and channel, category, status and owner, alongside a timeline of every event on the complaint in date order.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Timeline events seen: complaint received, acknowledgement sent, assigned, customer contacted, evidence requested, final response due.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Top left is the customer and their contact details, and on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need to add a note to a complaint that the system stamps with my name and today's date, so that there is a record of what I did.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You type in the box and press Add note, and it stamps your name and the date on it.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must not allow a saved note to be edited or deleted.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Notes are an audit trail.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Notes can't be edited or deleted once they're saved.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need to change a complaint's category on the Complaint Detail, and the system must require a note explaining why the category was changed.
requirement_candidates.rationale: The category is set by whoever logged the complaint and may be wrong.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: If it's wrong you can change it here, but you have to put a note in saying why.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must send a standard acknowledgement letter within 4 working days of receipt and record it as an event on the complaint timeline.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the timeline entry 'Acknowledgement sent — Standard acknowledgement letter, 4 working days'; the expert did not describe it.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must auto-assign a new complaint to a handler from a queue based on its category and record this on the timeline.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the timeline entry 'Assigned to Vibo Walridge — Auto-assigned from the Delayed claim queue'; the expert did not describe it.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need to record a decision by choosing one outcome (Uphold, Partially uphold or Reject), a reason from a dropdown, and a written summary of findings, so that the outcome is captured for the letter and reporting.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: It's three options: uphold, partially uphold, or reject. You pick one, choose a reason from the dropdown, and write the summary in the box.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must require the Summary of findings, count its words as the handler types, and not accept a decision until the summary is at least 50 words.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Word counter on screen reads 'At least 50 words. Currently 31 words.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The summary is mandatory and it has to be at least fifty words, the system counts them.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must allow only complaint handlers at grade 2 or above to record a decision; for trainees the Record decision button is disabled and a supervisor records it instead.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Banner on screen: 'Grade 2 and above. Only complaint handlers at grade 2 or above can record a decision. Trainees: ask your supervisor to record it.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Only complaint handlers at grade two and above can record a decision. If you're a trainee the button is greyed out and your supervisor records it for you.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a complaint handler, I need to save a decision as a draft before recording it, so that I can come back to it later.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the 'Save draft' button on screen; the expert did not describe it.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Then you press Record decision.

requirement_candidates.statement: For an upheld or partially upheld complaint, the system must not calculate redress until the handler has entered a Refund amount.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Redress calculation needs a refund amount to work from.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You put in the refund amount and the number of days the customer was out of pocket, and it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirement_candidates.statement: For an upheld or partially upheld complaint, the system must not calculate redress until the handler has entered the number of Days out of pocket.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Redress calculation needs the days figure to work from.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You put in the refund amount and the number of days the customer was out of pocket, and it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirement_candidates.statement: For an upheld or partially upheld complaint, the system calculates the interest and total redress from the Refund amount and the Days out of pocket.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You put in the refund amount and the number of days the customer was out of pocket, and it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must calculate interest as simple interest at the rate held in the Finance rate table, for the number of days out of pocket, and the rate must not be editable on the Redress screen.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Banner: 'Interest is simple interest at the Finance rate table figure, calculated from the number of days the customer was out of pocket.' On screen 750.00 at 8.00% for 90 days gives £14.79, consistent with 750 × 0.08 × 90/365.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The interest rate comes from somewhere in finance, I just use whatever it shows.

requirement_candidates.statement: When redress over £500 is approved, the system must require a second approval by the team lead and raise that as a task for the team lead.
requirement_candidates.rationale: On screen: 'Redress over £500 needs a second approver (team lead).'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Anything over five hundred pounds needs a second approver, and that pops up as a task for the team lead.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must generate the final response letter from a template, merging in the customer's name and address, the complaint reference, policy, product, received date, decision, summary of findings, redress amounts and handler name from the earlier screens, and highlight the merged fields in the preview.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Banner: 'Merge fields are highlighted.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: It's a template with the customer's name, the reference, the decision and the redress amount merged in from the earlier screens.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must not show the Send letter button until a decision has been recorded on the complaint.
requirement_candidates.rationale: On screen: 'Send letter appears only once a decision is recorded.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You can't send a letter until a decision is recorded, the Send letter button just won't show up.

requirement_candidates.statement: When the handler presses Send letter, the system must send the final response letter to print, or by email instead if the customer asked for email.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Banner: 'The letter is sent by post unless the customer asked for email.' The expert is not sure where the email preference is held.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: if it's right you press Send letter and it goes to print. If the customer asked for email, it's supposed to email it instead of printing.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a team lead, I need a Dashboard showing the team's open complaints, the number breaching the 8-week SLA, the uphold rate, and complaints received by month, so that I can monitor the team's workload and performance.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Three numbers: open complaints, how many are breaching SLA, and the uphold rate, and a chart of complaints received by month.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a team lead, I need to export the dashboard figures as a spreadsheet, so that I can use them outside the system.
requirement_candidates.rationale: On screen: 'Exports the figures above as a spreadsheet.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You press Export to get it all as a spreadsheet.

questions.question: Exactly how is SLA remaining calculated (from which date and time, calendar or working days, and what is the 8-week end point), and what is known about the cases where the clock is wrong?
questions.why_it_matters: The SLA drives the sort order, the Breached flag, the automatic Ombudsman referral and the dashboard; the expert says the current clock is sometimes wrong, so the rule must be pinned down rather than copied.
questions.context_quote: Sometimes the SLA clock is wrong, honestly, nobody knows why, so you double-check the received date.

questions.question: What does the automatic Ombudsman referral actually do beyond changing the status to Referred: is anything sent to the Ombudsman or the customer, who is notified, and can a handler still work the complaint afterwards?
questions.why_it_matters: A developer needs to know whether this is a status change or an integration with an external body and what happens to the complaint after it.
questions.context_quote: Anything over eight weeks old goes to the Ombudsman automatically, you'll see the status flip to Referred on its own.

questions.question: What defines 'your team' for the inbox, and why does it include a row with Owner 'Unassigned' and a row owned by Dalo Walwell? Can a handler see other teams' complaints?
questions.why_it_matters: The inbox filter is the first thing a handler sees; the visibility rule decides who can see and pick up which complaints.
questions.context_quote: You land on the Inbox, which is every open complaint sorted by how long we've got left on it.

questions.question: What is the full list of statuses (New, Investigating, Awaiting customer, Decided, Referred were seen) and what moves a complaint from one to the next: is it done by hand or by the system when a decision is recorded, a letter is sent, and so on?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert never described how status changes; without the transitions the workflow cannot be built.
questions.context_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

questions.question: How do Owner and 'Assigned to' relate? On the frame the Owner is Mabo Grawell but the timeline says the complaint was auto-assigned to Vibo Walridge. How does auto-assignment from a category queue work and can a complaint be reassigned by hand?
questions.why_it_matters: Ownership decides whose inbox the complaint appears in and who is responsible for the deadline.
questions.context_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

questions.question: Is the note explaining a category change enforced by the system (for example a mandatory reason box when pressing Change) or is it a team rule the handler is expected to follow?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the developer must build a validation or only document a process.
questions.context_quote: If it's wrong you can change it here, but you have to put a note in saying why.

questions.question: Does 'notes cannot be edited or deleted' apply to every user including supervisors and administrators, and is there any way to correct a note entered by mistake (for example adding a correcting note)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the permissions model for the audit trail and what to do about genuine mistakes.
questions.context_quote: Notes can't be edited or deleted once they're saved.

questions.question: Is the acknowledgement letter sent automatically by the system within 4 working days of receipt, or by a person, and what template and channel does it use?
questions.why_it_matters: The timeline shows an acknowledgement event but the expert did not cover it; if it is automatic it is a scheduled job the developer must build.
questions.context_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

questions.question: What are all the options in the Reason dropdown, and do they depend on the outcome or category chosen?
questions.why_it_matters: Only one value ('Delay not fully explained') was visible; the list is reference data the developer must load.
questions.context_quote: You pick one, choose a reason from the dropdown, and write the summary in the box.

questions.question: How are words counted for the 50-word minimum (numbers, hyphenated words, references like CMP-2026-01518), and is there a maximum length for the summary?
questions.why_it_matters: The count decides whether Record decision is allowed, so the counting rule must be exact.
questions.context_quote: The summary is mandatory and it has to be at least fifty words, the system counts them.

questions.question: How does the system know a handler's grade (a role, a user attribute, an HR feed)? When a supervisor records a decision for a trainee, is it recorded under the supervisor's name or the trainee's, and can a decision be changed after it is recorded?
questions.why_it_matters: Needed to build the permission check and to attribute decisions correctly for audit and the uphold-rate figures.
questions.context_quote: If you're a trainee the button is greyed out and your supervisor records it for you.

questions.question: What does Save draft save, who can see a draft decision, and does a draft count as 'a decision is recorded' for the purposes of showing the Send letter button?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert did not mention drafts; the developer needs to know the draft lifecycle and that a draft must not unlock the letter.
questions.context_quote: Then you press Record decision.

questions.question: Where does the Finance rate table live and how does the system read it: is it a table in this system, a feed from a finance system, and which rate applies when the rate changes (the rate on the day of calculation, or the rate over the period out of pocket)?
questions.why_it_matters: The interest figure goes into the customer's letter and payment; the source and versioning of the rate must be defined.
questions.context_quote: The interest rate comes from somewhere in finance, I just use whatever it shows.

questions.question: What is the exact interest formula: day-count basis (365 or 366 days in a leap year), rounding rule, and is interest applied to the refund amount only?
questions.why_it_matters: The figures on screen (750.00 at 8% for 90 days = £14.79) fit 365-day simple interest, but the rounding and leap-year handling were not stated and affect what the customer is paid.
questions.context_quote: it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

questions.question: When redress over £500 needs a second approver, what happens next: does the complaint wait until the team lead approves, can the letter be sent before that, who counts as the team lead, and what happens if the team lead rejects or changes the amount? Is the £500 threshold on the total redress or the refund only?
questions.why_it_matters: This is a control on paying money out; the developer needs the full approval workflow, not just the trigger.
questions.context_quote: Anything over five hundred pounds needs a second approver, and that pops up as a task for the team lead.

questions.question: For a rejected complaint, or a partially upheld complaint with no money owed, is the Redress screen skipped, and does the letter template change to leave out the payment paragraph?
questions.why_it_matters: The walkthrough only showed the partially upheld path with a payment; the other outcomes need their own path through redress and the letter.
questions.context_quote: If it's upheld or partially upheld, you go to Redress.

questions.question: Where is the customer's preference for email over post held, and how does the system read it when Send letter is pressed?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert says email is supposed to happen instead of print but the preference is not on any screen shown, so the source of that data is unknown.
questions.context_quote: If the customer asked for email, it's supposed to email it instead of printing. I'm not sure where that preference is set, it's not on any of these screens.

questions.question: What does 'goes to print' mean technically (a print queue, a mailing house, a PDF), is a copy of the sent letter stored on the complaint, and does sending the letter change the complaint status or close it?
questions.why_it_matters: Sending the final response is the end of the process and the developer needs to know the integration and what record it leaves.
questions.context_quote: You read it through, and if it's right you press Send letter and it goes to print.

questions.question: Who is allowed to use Edit template, and does it change the template for every future letter or only the letter for this complaint? Are the fixed sentences (payment within 10 working days, Ombudsman referral within six months) regulatory wording that must not be editable?
questions.why_it_matters: Editing a template that is used for regulated final responses needs clear ownership and controls.
questions.context_quote: It's a template with the customer's name, the reference, the decision and the redress amount merged in from the earlier screens.

questions.question: Over what period is the uphold rate calculated (this calendar month, a rolling window, or all time), and is it based on decisions recorded or complaints received in that period?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert is unsure; the figure is a headline team-performance measure and its definition must be agreed before it is built.
questions.context_quote: I think the uphold rate is this month, but it might be rolling, I've never checked.

questions.question: Who can see the Dashboard, and how is the team it shows chosen? The frame shows a grade 2 handler viewing 'Team view for Dalo Walwell's team' although the expert says it is for the team lead.
questions.why_it_matters: Decides access control for the dashboard and whether a handler can see teams other than their own.
questions.context_quote: Dashboard is what the team lead looks at.

questions.question: What exactly does Export contain and in what format: the three headline figures, the monthly counts, or the underlying complaint list, and how many months of history?
questions.why_it_matters: The screen only says 'Exports the figures above as a spreadsheet'; the developer needs the file layout.
questions.context_quote: You press Export to get it all as a spreadsheet.

questions.question: What are the Reports and Settings pages in the left navigation, and how is a complaint first logged (the walkthrough starts with complaints already in the inbox)?
questions.why_it_matters: Two navigation items and the logging step were never shown, so the scope of the system is bigger than the walkthrough covers.
questions.context_quote: That's the whole process, inbox to letter.
